$comment: Brand content for the catalog: what Fourthwall doesn't hold (internal design code, release, position, category, Scripture, copy). When a product's slug (or fourthwallSlug) matches a Fourthwall product, Fourthwall supplies its variants, prices, stock and photos. Until then the product shows as a preview: the price, sizes and images here (apps/web/public/products, styled mockups made by assets/mockups), with ordering not yet open. `scripture` is each piece's shared Scripture record: the website shows one translation (SCRIPTURE_TRANSLATION, NIV by default) everywhere the piece appears. `code` is internal and never shown to customers. `colors` maps garment color names to brand swatch tokens. `images` are listed in display order: listing image (the whole garment), hover image, then the rest.

collections.name: Behold
collections.tagline: A call to see Christ’s power, holiness, sacrifice, and resurrection.
collections.story: Behold means look, and keep looking. When John the Baptist saw Jesus coming toward him, he called everyone near him to see the Lamb of God, and older English Bibles begin his words with “Behold.” These seven pieces carry the same call: see His holiness, His power over the storm, His mercy, the veil torn open by His death, His resurrection, the life He gives, and the Lamb who takes away the sin of the world.

scripture.niv: Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.
scripture.kjv: Put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.

story.art: The bush that burned and was not consumed, its roots spread wide over the desert floor beneath the wordmark.
story.meaning: Moses turned aside to look at a bush that was on fire but did not burn up, and God called to him from the flames. Before anything else, God told him where he was standing: holy ground. The design keeps that order. The fire rises over everything, the roots hold the ground beneath it, and the reference sits at the hem.
story.front: Small Awebound wordmark with a single flame, left chest; flame mark on the left sleeve
story.back: Awebound wordmark over the burning bush, its roots and the desert hills
story.fit: Regular tee · classic fit, set-in sleeves

scripture.niv: They were terrified and asked each other, “Who is this? Even the wind and the waves obey him!”
scripture.kjv: And they feared exceedingly, and said one to another, What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?

story.art: Storm clouds break over a raging sea, and on the horizon a cross stands in the light.
story.meaning: The disciples were fishermen who knew that sea, and the storm still frightened them. Jesus spoke to the wind and the waves, and everything went still. What stayed with them was the question that followed: who is this? The front shows the storm breaking around a cross on the horizon. The back carries the disciples’ question in full.
story.front: Awebound wordmark over the storm, the waves and the cross on the horizon
story.back: The words of Mark 4:41 in engraved capitals, in the King James wording, above a breaking wave
story.fit: Larger oversized · dropped shoulder, extra-boxy body

scripture.niv: Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow
scripture.kjv: Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow

story.art: A crown of thorns breaks into lilies, framing the wordmark beneath a cross.
story.meaning: Through Isaiah, God calls His people to come and settle the matter, and promises that sins as deep as scarlet will be made white as snow. The crown of thorns is the cost of that mercy, and the lilies are what grows from it. Deep red on a bone shirt: scarlet and snow, worn together.
story.front: Large Awebound wordmark across the chest in deep red
story.back: Crown of thorns blooming into lilies around the wordmark and Isaiah 1:18
story.fit: Larger oversized · dropped shoulder, extra-boxy body

scripture.niv: At that moment the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
scripture.kjv: And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom

story.art: A red temple curtain torn from top to bottom, light pouring through the tear above the clouds, beneath the words “The veil is torn.”
story.meaning: When Jesus gave up His spirit on the cross, the curtain in the temple, the veil that closed off the Most Holy Place, was torn in two from top to bottom. Torn from the top down, it was opened from God’s side: through Christ’s death, the way into His presence stands open. The back shows the curtain torn wide with light breaking through; the front keeps only the wordmark.
story.front: Awebound wordmark in bone with red thorns, center chest
story.back: “The veil is torn” in heavy gothic capitals above a red curtain torn open, light breaking through over the clouds, with Matthew 27:51 below
story.fit: Relaxed hoodie · dropped shoulder, kangaroo pocket, ribbed cuffs and hem

scripture.niv: He is not here; he has risen, just as he said. Come and see the place where he lay.
scripture.kjv: He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.

story.art: The stone rolls away in a sweep of blue beneath the angel’s announcement.
story.meaning: Early on the first day of the week, the women came to the tomb and found the stone rolled away. The angel told them Jesus was not there: He had risen, just as He said. The back sets the angel’s announcement in heavy capitals, as plain as news, with the stone still rolling in a sweep of blue below it. The front keeps only the wordmark.
story.back: “He is not here: for he is risen” in heavy capitals (Matthew 28:6, King James wording) above the stone rolling away in a sweep of blue
story.fit: Regular oversized · dropped shoulder, boxy body

products.name: To Live Is Christ, To Die Is Gain

scripture.niv: For to me, to live is Christ and to die is gain.
scripture.kjv: For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain.

story.art: An hourglass holds a cross above and a sprouting seed below, between the words of Philippians 1:21.
story.meaning: Paul wrote these words in chains, not knowing whether he would live or die, and found that either way he could not lose. The hourglass holds a cross above and a sprouting seed below: time running out, and a life that goes on. To live is to live for Christ; to die is to be with Him.
story.front: To live is Christ, to die is gain, set around the hourglass
story.back: Small Awebound wordmark below the collar
story.fit: Regular oversized · dropped shoulder, boxy body

To Live Is Christ oversized tee, back: small wordmark below the collar

scripture.niv: Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!
scripture.kjv: Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.

story.art: The Lamb of God, embroidered in raised bone thread across the front panel.
story.meaning: When John the Baptist saw Jesus coming toward him, he named Him: the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world. It is the call this whole release is named for. The lamb is embroidered in raised bone thread with a single mark of red, and the reference sits on the side of the cap.
story.front: Raised embroidered lamb in bone thread
story.back: Awebound wordmark with red thorns above the snap; John 1:29 on the side
story.fit: Otto mid-profile snapback · structured crown, adjustable snap
